heading: Course Description
text: Climate change one defining challenges 21st century, influencing ecosystems, biodiversity, food production, water resources, human health, many aspects environment. two-term capstone course provides ENVS ENSC majors opportunity synthesize knowledge gained throughout undergraduate studies apply real-world climate change questions. Rather introducing climate change stand-alone topic, course examines environmental processes lens climate change equips students quantitative tools needed investigate . fall term, students develop toolkit evidence-based climate assessment. winter term, students work small groups climate-related research project choice. combine concepts analytical approaches introduced fall term investigate real-world problem, impacts climate change biodiversity, wildfires, drought, food systems, climate adaptation mitigation strategies. course concludes public Project Symposium, students present findings peers faculty.

heading: 1.12 Quantifying the warming trend
text: plot shows global mean surface temperature increased substantially since 1850. can use simple linear model quantify trend. following code fits linear relationship GMST year:coefficient associated year represents estimated change GMST per year. can extract model coefficients using:second coefficient estimated change GMST per year. can multiply 100 express trend degrees Celsius per century.Quiz Question: estimated rate global warming degrees Celsius per century entire 1850–2024 period?
code:
model <- lm(GMST ~ year, data = data)
summary(model)
coef(model)
coef(model)[2] * 100

heading: 1.13 Has the rate of warming changed?
text: single trend 175 years assumes rate warming constant. can investigate whether assumption reasonable calculating trends different periods. First, create dataset containing observations 1850 1950 onlyQuiz Question: estimated warming rate per century 1850 1950?Quiz Question: estimated warming rate per century 1950 2024?
code:
early <- data[data$year >= 1850 & data$year <= 1950, ]
early_model <- lm(GMST ~ year, data = early)
early_trend <- coef(early_model)[2] * 100
print(early_trend)
